newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan GDP grows slightly in July-September quarter.
newsitem.headline: Japan GDP grows slightly in July-September quarter.

text.p: Japan's economy grew slightly in the three months to September after contracting in the previous quarter, the government said on Tuesday.

The government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said gross domestic product (GDP) -- a key gauge of the economy's health -- rose a real 0.1 percent in the July-September period from the previous quarter. This translated into a rise of 0.4 percent on an annualised basis, it said.

GDP, which measures the country's output of goods and services minus net income from overseas production, fell a real 0.7 percent in the April-June period from the previous quarter, or 2.9 percent on an annualised basis.
Economists polled by Reuters had been divided over whether the data would show a modest decline or some growth. Forecasts had ranged from an annualised fall of 3.8 percent to a rise of 1.2 percent.
But they agreed that weak personal consumption and a fall-off in public works spending had kept the economy relatively weak.

Analysts had said especially weak data would have intensified Japan's debate about the need to spend more out of public coffers to keep the recovery on track. The Finance Ministry is opposed to such a move because it places priority on efforts to reduce the nation's huge budget deficit.
